thread:
deploy-bot: Scheduled deployment 'frontend-canary v2.3.1' for 2026-03-20 22:00 UTC. Rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Targets: hosted API (US, EU, APAC). Change window 22:00-23:30 UTC. Release manager: @emma. React with :thumbsup: to proceed or reply to modify.

emma: Heads up — incident open in EU-west affecting GPU scheduler. Ops oncall pinged. Recommend we hold EU path until we verify node stability. Not safe to push new binaries to EU right now.

ops-oncall: Confirming, seeing scheduler backlog + repeated driver resets on 3 EU nodes. Symptoms: short-lived CUDA_init failures causing worker restarts. Impact: intermittent inference failures for small requests. Dedicated clusters unaffected (different tenancy). Investigating; throttling new tasks to affected nodes.

henry: Is that only hosted? Any error logs we can look at to decide whether to proceed excluding EU?

ops-oncall: Primarily hosted. Pasting recent log snippet:
```
2026-03-20T20:12:43Z gpu-sched ERROR node-12: cuda_init failed: driver: 0x3e
2026-03-20T20:12:44Z worker-88 WARN reconnecting to node-12
2026-03-20T20:12:46Z gpu-sched INFO backlog=84 pending_jobs=12
```

emma: Ok. Plan proposal: hard hold EU region, pin EU route to current stable version (2.3.0), and proceed with canary in US + APAC at 22:00. Manual gate before EU rollforward. @deploy-bot can you enact hold and pin?

deploy-bot: Actioning: pinning 'frontend-service:2.3.0' for route eu-west. EU deploy path set to HOLD. Canary will proceed in US+APAC only at 22:00 UTC with manual approval required for EU. To rollback/pin manually:
```
# pin EU to 2.3.0
rwdctl routes pin --service frontend --version 2.3.0 --region eu-west
# rollback example
rwdctl deploy rollback --service frontend --version 2.3.0 --region eu-west
```
Done: hold applied and pin created. Notifying watchers.

maria: I'll update release notes to say EU delayed due to infra incident; will include follow-up ETA. QA: please keep smoke tests on hold for EU until ops clears.

sam: Can we reschedule EU rollforward to 2026-03-20 23:45-00:30 UTC so ops has time to clear, or do we push to tomorrow morning? If ops ETA > 1hr I'd prefer morning.

ops-oncall: ETA ~45 minutes to stabilize nodes, but full confidence tomorrow morning. Recommend moving EU rollforward to 2026-03-21 10:00 UTC to avoid repeated flapping.

emma: Agreed. I'll update the release calendar and notify customers on the EU pilot list. maria, please add a short blurb to release notes explaining the delay.

maria: Added note: "EU region rollforward delayed due to GPU scheduler incident. EU will remain on 2.3.0 until verified. Target rollforward: 2026-03-21 10:00 UTC (subject to ops confirmation)."

henry: After pin/hold, we should add a temporary monitor: alert on p95 latency and 5xx rate for 60 minutes post-canary in US/APAC and on any backlog in the scheduler. If any regressions, we abort and rollback.

emma: Good call. @henry please create the dashboard/alert and set an automatic abort threshold for canary (5xx > 1% or p95 > +150ms baseline).

henry: Will do, creating the monitor now and will attach the runbook link.

deploy-bot: Deployment proceeding in US+APAC at 22:00 UTC. EU pinned to 2.3.0 and EU rollforward scheduled for 2026-03-21 10:00 UTC pending ops confirmation. Watchers: @emma @maria @henry @ops-oncall. Logs will stream to #eng-releases.

emma: :thumbsup: Thanks team. I'll post a brief customer note and close the loop once ops confirms. If timeline changes, I'll update here.
